Quarterly National Accounts of Spain – Q3 2026, complete/final figures

release_schedule.note: INE's official advance-release calendar (dynt3/Calendario) lists dated releases for the statistical operation 'Quarterly Spanish National Accounts' (cid=1254736164439), which is the operation actually matching this report's releases_per_year=4 (quarterly) periodicity — the corpus's current url field (oper=344) instead points to the metadata page for 'Annual National Accounts of Spain: main aggregates', a related but distinct annual operation with a different (preliminary/provisional/final over 3 years) publication pattern. For the Quarterly National Accounts, INE actually publishes each quarter's GDP figures twice — an 'Avance'/Preview about one month after quarter-end, then complete/final figures about three months after quarter-end — so the full calendar shows 8 dated releases per year (2 per quarter), not 4. Confirmed dates for 2026 pulled directly from the calendar page: Jan 30 (Avance Q4/2025), Mar 26 (Q4/2025 final), Apr 30 (Preview Q1/2026), Jun 25 (Q1/2026 final), Jul 30 (Preview Q2/2026, matches the actual Jul 30 2026 press release found), Sep 25 (Q2/2026 final), Oct 30 (Preview Q3/2026), Dec 23 (Q3/2026 final).

reports.title: Volkswirtschaftliche Gesamtrechnungen / National accounts (ESA 2010)
reports.description: Austrian national accounts compiled according to the requirements of ESA 2010.

entries.covers: GDP and main aggregates, full year 2026 and 4th quarter 2026 (preliminary)

release_schedule.note: Statistik Austria's national accounts (VGR) programme, of which quarterly GDP and main aggregates is the flagship indicator, is released on a quarterly cadence (~64-67 days after quarter end). The publisher's own statistics page lists a 'Nächste Veröffentlichungen' (next publications) block with these exact upcoming dates. Cross-checked against past releases confirming the pattern: Q1 2026 released 2026-06-03, Q4 2025/annual 2025 released 2026-03-05, Q3 2025 released 2025-12-04, Q2 2025 released 2025-09-05.

release_schedule.note: Statistics Estonia publishes detailed quarterly National accounts (ESA 2010) data roughly 60 days after quarter-end, confirmed via the publisher's own filterable release calendar (theme = 'National accounts') at stat.ee for the whole of 2026: 2026-03-02 (Q4 2025), 2026-05-29 (Q1 2026), 2026-08-31 (Q2 2026), 2026-11-30 (Q3 2026) — 4 releases/year, consistent with releases_per_year=4 on file. This is distinct from the earlier 'GDP flash estimate (ESA 2010)' releases (e.g. 2026-07-30 for Q2 2026), which are a separate, faster preliminary product on the same calendar. A revision release for 2022-2025 data was also scheduled for 2026-08-14 (3 days from today), but that is a revision of historical data rather than the next new-period release.

release_schedule.note: BFS publishes a single comprehensive annual national accounts release each year (press release 'Volkswirtschaftliche Gesamtrechnung der Schweiz im Jahr X', covering GDP by three approaches, sector accounts, government accounts, ESA2010/ESVG2010 framework), roughly 8-14 months after the reference year ends. No published release calendar or stated rule was found on bfs.admin.ch giving an exact date; the August-September timing is inferred from three consecutive years of actual releases (24 Aug 2023 for 2022 data, 27 Aug 2024 for 2023 data, 29 Sep 2025 for 2024 data - the last one delayed, likely due to a methodology/benchmark revision reported in Swiss media). Note: quarterly GDP estimates for Switzerland are produced by SECO (Staatssekretariat für Wirtschaft), not BFS - SECO's 'Bruttoinlandprodukt - Quartalsschätzung' is a separate, distinct product from this BFS annual national accounts report. The corpus's releases_per_year=4 for this specific BFS report does not match what was found; see existing_field_correction.

reports.title: National accounts (ESA 2010)
reports.publisher: Statistical Office of the Republic of Serbia (SORS/RZS)
reports.description: Serbian national accounts. As an EU candidate country, SORS's own language describes alignment as an ongoing process rather than a binding legal obligation — the first documented instance of a third, weaker category of relationship language in this branch.

reports.title: UK National Accounts / Blue Book
reports.description: UK national accounts. The UK was bound by ESA 2010 as an EU member until 2020; the 2025 Blue Book states in the present tense that the UK "still follows" the ESA 2010 framework — voluntary post-Brexit continuity for international comparability, not a dead arrangement.

reports.title: Échelle mobile des salaires (automatic wage indexation)
reports.description: Luxembourg's statutory automatic wage-indexation mechanism (Loi du 25 mars 2015), which adjusts wages and salaries periodically whenever STATEC's published consumer price index crosses a defined threshold.

dependencies.basis: "This statistical operation adopts the methodology contained in the European System of Economic Accounts (SEC-2010) in compliance with the provisions of Regulation (EU) No. 549/2013 of the European Parliament and the Council, of May 21..." / "Este nuevo estándar metodológico... fue adoptado mediante el Reglamento (UE) Nº 549/2013... y, por lo tanto, de obligado cumplimiento para todos los estados miembros de la Unión."

"National accounts data concern all data produced and disseminated for an economy according to the definitions and guidelines of the European System of Accounts (ESA 2010). As the data for all reference periods are compiled according to the requirements of the ESA 2010..."

"Since the publication in September 2014, the Swedish National Accounts are produced fully in accordance with the ESA 2010 principles for the period 1993 and onwards. The National Accounts follow the European System of National and Regional Accounts, (ESA 2010), which is an internationally comparable accounting system and applies as law in Member States."
"Statistics Estonia compiles national accounts according to the concepts, definitions, classifications and accounting rules of the European System of Accounts (ESA 2010)."

"Iceland has an obligation under the EEA agreement to comply with the EU's guidelines for national accounts statistics. EEA countries are required to implement the ESA 2010 by September 2014. As from 2014 the Icelandic national accounts are compiled in accordance with the guidelines in the European System of Accounts (ESA 2010)."

"Basis für die Berechnungen ist das Europäische System Volkswirtschaftlicher Gesamtrechnungen (ESVG 2010). Es enthält die grundlegenden Konzepte und Definitionen sowie Buchungsregeln zur Erstellung Volkswirtschaftlicher Gesamtrechnungen." ("The basis for the calculations is the European System of Accounts (ESA 2010). It contains the fundamental concepts and definitions as well as the accounting rules for compiling national accounts.")

"The Statistics Agreement includes the obligation to state the most important financial statistics aggregates at a macroeconomic level according to the rules and standards of the ESA 2010. Switzerland's system of national accounts... is based on the ESA 2010..."

"In order to establish an efficient statistical system in the field of national accounts, which will be harmonised with the relevant EU legislation... further the process of modernization of official statistics on the way to harmonization with the methodology and practice of the European Union... The balancing process is performed in accordance with ESA 2010 main recommendations." Aspirational alignment language, not binding obligation — relationship_type recorded as cites rather than methodology_depends_on because Serbia is not legally bound the way member and EEA/bilateral states are; flag for review at the other end of the process.

"Within the European System of Accounts (ESA) 2010, which the UK still follows..." / "Defined and classified according to the European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010)." Present tense, five years after the UK's EU membership ended in 2020 — voluntary continuity for international comparability, not a description of a dead arrangement.

"Le traitement est adapté périodiquement aux variations du coût de la vie constaté par l'indice pondéré des prix à la consommation qui est établi et publié chaque mois par l'Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques." ("Treatment is adapted periodically to variations in the cost of living as recorded by the weighted consumer price index established and published monthly by STATEC.") Statute cites the index by its base-1948 linkage and monthly publication cadence, not by the IPCH/IPCN acronym; separate STATEC methodology pages identify IPCN, not IPCH, as the index used for the sliding wage scale.

_dropped.why: Statbel itself makes no direct statement that it compiles national accounts under ESA 2010 — searches on statbel.fgov.be for 'SEC 2010' / 'ESA 2010' / 'comptes nationaux' returned nothing. Belgian national accounts are actually produced by the Institut des comptes nationaux, housed at the National Bank of Belgium, which DOES use binding language ('établis selon les prescrits du SEC 2010'). See the round-7 slice, where the correct source (NBB/ICN) is used instead.
